41/**
42 * @brief Strategy for ensuring positive semi-definite (PSD) Hessian matrices in material models.
43 *
44 * @details The material Hessian (∂P/∂F, where P is the first Piola-Kirchhoff stress and F is the
45 * deformation gradient) should be PSD for stable simulation. This enum defines strategies to
46 * enforce this property, balancing computational cost against stability and convergence quality.
47 *
48 * @note Different materials support different strategies. Check material-specific documentation.
49 *
50 * @see SoftMaterialType
51 */
52enum struct MaterialPsdStrategy {
53 /**
54 * @brief Use the material's default PSD strategy.
55 *
56 * @note Supported for all material models.
57 * @note Each material model defines its own recommended default strategy.
58 */
59 MaterialDefault,
60
61 /**
62 * @brief No PSD enforcement. Negative eigenvalues may arise.
63 *
64 * @details Fastest strategy but may substantially degrade stability of most material models.
65 *
66 * @note Supported for all material models.
67 */
68 None,
69
70 /**
71 * @brief Eigenvalue clamping: U * Max(Λ, ε) * U^T.
72 *
73 * @details Performs eigendecomposition ∂P/∂F = U * Λ * U^T and clamps negative eigenvalues to a
74 * small positive constant ε. Slower than most other methods, but typically ensures best
75 * convergence.
76 *
77 * @note Supported for all material models.
78 *
79 * @see materials::kMinProjectedEigenvalue
80 */
81 Projection,
82
83 /**
84 * @brief Fast PSD enforcement by dropping problematic terms.
85 *
86 * @details Faster than @ref MaterialPsdStrategy::Projection but may degrade non-linear solver
87 * convergence.
88 *
89 * @note Only supported for @ref SoftMaterialType::StVenantKirchhoff and @ref
90 * SoftMaterialType::NeoHookean materials.
91 *
92 * @warning For @ref SoftMaterialType::StVenantKirchhoff, does not guarantee a PSD Hessian when
93 * the Poisson ratio is negative (auxetic materials). Use @ref MaterialPsdStrategy::Projection or
94 * @ref MaterialPsdStrategy::AbsEigenProjection instead.
95 */
96 Fast,
97
98 /**
99 * @brief Absolute eigenvalue projection: U * Max(|Λ|, ε) * U^T.
100 *
101 * @details Takes absolute value of eigenvalues instead of clamping. Similar cost to @ref
102 * MaterialPsdStrategy::Projection but may improve stability, especially for highly deformed
103 * configurations.
104 *
105 * @note Supported for all material models.
106 *
107 * @see [Stabler Neo-Hookean Simulation: Absolute Eigenvalue Filtering for Projected Newton (Chen
108 * et al., 2024)](https://www.cs.columbia.edu/cg/abs-psd/paper.pdf)
109 * @see materials::kMinProjectedEigenvalue
110 */
111 AbsEigenProjection,
112
113 /**
114 * @brief Per-term projection for composite Hessians.
115 *
116 * @details Projects each summand of the Hessian separately. For example, if H = H1 + H2, projects
117 * both H1 and H2 independently.
118 *
119 * @note Only supported for @ref SoftMaterialType::ActiveShapeTargetingArap material.
120 */
121 PerTermProjection,
122
123 /** @brief Number of unique enum values. */
124 Count,
125};
126} // namespace superdex
127
128MOCHI_ENUM_BEGIN(superdex::MaterialPsdStrategy)
129MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(MaterialDefault)
130MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(None)
131MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(Projection)
132MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(Fast)
133MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(AbsEigenProjection)
134MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(PerTermProjection)
135MOCHI_ENUM_COUNT(Count)
136MOCHI_ENUM_END()

138namespace superdex {
139/**
140 * @brief Material constitutive models for soft bodies.
141 *
142 * @details Defines the constitutive response for deformable materials (strain energy and
143 * stress-strain relationship). Each material has different mechanical properties, computational
144 * cost, and stability characteristics.
145 *
146 * @see SoftMaterialParams, MaterialPsdStrategy
147 */
148enum struct SoftMaterialType {
149 /**
150 * @brief Neo-Hookean hyperelastic material.
151 *
152 * @details Non-linear hyperelastic material with log-barrier stabilization to handle extreme
153 * deformations and element inversions robustly. Recommended for most soft body simulations
154 * requiring large deformations.
155 *
156 * @see [Stable Neo-Hookean Flesh Simulation (Smith et al.,
157 * 2018)](https://www.tkim.graphics/NEO/StableNeoHookean2018.pdf)
158 * @see NeoHookeanMaterialParams
159 */
160 NeoHookean = 0,
161
162 /**
163 * @brief Saint Venant-Kirchhoff (StVK) hyperelastic material.
164 *
165 * @details Classical non-linear hyperelastic material. Simpler than neo-Hookean but may exhibit
166 * instabilities under large deformations, particularly under large compression.
167 *
168 * @see StVenantKirchhoffMaterialParams
169 */
170 StVenantKirchhoff = 1,
171
172 /**
173 * @brief Linear elastic material (Hookean).
174 *
175 * @details Simplest material model with linear stress-strain relationship. Computationally fast
176 * but only accurate for small deformations.
177 *
178 * @note Not suitable for large deformations.
179 * @note No PSD enforcement is needed. The Hessian matrix is positive definite regardless of the
180 * PSD strategy.
181 *
182 * @see LinearElasticMaterialParams
183 */
184 LinearElastic = 2,
185
186 /**
187 * @brief Composite material: passive isotropic elasticity + active anisotropic fiber actuation.
188 *
189 * @details Combines a passive isotropic hyperelastic component (Neo-Hookean) with an active
190 * anisotropic fiber contraction component (Aniso ARAP). Used to model materials with directional
191 * actuation like muscle tissue.
192 *
193 * @see [Stable Neo-Hookean Flesh Simulation (Smith et al.,
194 * 2018)](https://www.tkim.graphics/NEO/StableNeoHookean2018.pdf)
195 * @see [Anisotropic Elasticity for Inversion-Safety and Element Rehabilitation (Kim et al.,
196 * 2019)](http://tkim.graphics/ANISOTROPY/AnisotropyAndRehab.pdf)
197 * @see ActiveNeoHookeanMaterialParams
198 */
199 ActiveNeoHookean = 3,
200
201 /**
202 * @brief Active As-Rigid-As-Possible (ARAP) material with Shape Targeting.
203 *
204 * @details Active material model based on the concept of "shape targeting". Unlike passive models
205 * that only react to external loads, it introduces an internal actuation mechanism.
206 *
207 * The actuation is defined by the shape target tensor, S_t, which specifies the desired local
208 * shape of the object. The model then resists deformation from this target shape while allowing
209 * rigid rotation.
210 *
211 * This approach is effective for simulating biological phenomena like muscle contraction.
212 *
213 * @note The "activeness" is controlled externally by setting the shape target tensor S_t. The
214 * model itself does not have an intrinsic, self-actuating mechanism without this input.
215 *
216 * @see [Shape Targeting: A Versatile Active Elasticity Constitutive Model (Klár et al.,
217 * 2020)](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10230451)
218 * @see ActiveShapeTargetingArapMaterialParams
219 */
220 ActiveShapeTargetingArap = 4,
221
222 /**
223 * @brief As-Rigid-As-Possible (ARAP) material.
224 *
225 * @details ARAP's primary goal is to deform the object such that each local region undergoes a
226 * transformation that is as close to a rigid rotation as possible.
227 *
228 * Because it preserves local shape details well and produces intuitive, natural-looking results,
229 * ARAP is widely used in computer graphics for applications like interactive mesh editing and
230 * character posing.
231 *
232 * @see [Dynamic Deformables (Kim and Eberle,
233 * 2022)](https://www.tkim.graphics/DYNAMIC_DEFORMABLES/DynamicDeformables.pdf)
234 * @see ArapMaterialParams
235 */
236 Arap = 5,
237
238 /** @brief Number of unique material type enum values. */
239 Count = 6
240};
241} // namespace superdex
242
243MOCHI_ENUM_BEGIN(superdex::SoftMaterialType);
244MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(NeoHookean) MOCHI_ATTRIBUTE(PreviouslyKnownAs("StableNeoHookean"));
245MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(StVenantKirchhoff);
246MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(LinearElastic);
247MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(ActiveNeoHookean) MOCHI_ATTRIBUTE(PreviouslyKnownAs("ActiveStableNeoHookean"));
248MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(ActiveShapeTargetingArap);
249MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(Arap);
250MOCHI_ENUM_COUNT(Count);
251MOCHI_ENUM_END();

253namespace superdex::materials {

255/// @brief Opt-in trait: a material params type declares this @c true iff its reference (@c F=I)
256/// tangent is isotropic — i.e. invariant under rotation, so it is fully described by the two Lamé
257/// scalars (λ, μ) with no directional coupling.
258///
259/// @details The primary template is @c false. A material specializes it to @c true only when this
260/// holds by construction, independently of the specific parameter values. Consumers may optionally
261/// use it to take faster, isotropy-specific code paths where applicable; leaving it @c false is
262/// always correct and simply forgoes those paths.
263template <class ParamsT>
264inline constexpr bool kIsotropicReferenceStiffness = false;
265
266} // namespace superdex::materials
